G3-NAV-001.defect: Reference path byte-budget admission is based on the actual prepared path shape, including cost-provider midpoint expansion.

G3-NAV-002.defect: A successful backend/reference result remains owned across local budget/allocation failure and retry does not call the backend again.

G3-NAV-003.defect: Released/expired query purge occurs only after all fallible purge/query work-list preparation succeeds.

G3-PHYS-001.defect: Tick uses prefix-progress acceptance: accepted delta/prefix and backend simulation are not replayed after a later fixed-step synchronization/projection failure.

G3-SIM-001.defect: Successful ExecuteStep output is durably owned before fallible local publication and retry does not call the job twice.

G3-SIM-002.defect: Post-commit pruning/result bookkeeping is allocation-safe so late local allocation cannot make an accepted prefix ambiguous.

G3-SIM-AUDIT-001.defect: Once retryable shutdown starts, new Tick/Schedule/main-thread/proposal work is rejected while cleanup ownership remains retryable.

G3-SIM-AUDIT-002.defect: SetAttention contains first-insertion allocation failure in Result and preserves prior attention state.

G3-SIM-AUDIT-003.defect: Proposal Publish contains allocation failure and leaves the proposal queue unchanged.

G3-STR-001.defect: Runtime-local Tick preparation/allocation failure must propagate before mutation rather than becoming a semantic request failure.

G3-STR-002.defect: A successful ExecuteStep result is accepted exactly once and retained across later local commit failure so retry does not execute the backend step twice.

G3-STR-003.defect: A Commit step in a progressive plan is unique and terminal, preventing external commit before later work.

G3-STR-004.defect: Request publication rollback restores prior chunk state/mapping and identity allocators when later publication fails.

M3C-PHYS-001.defect: Finite large ray directions are normalized with sufficient range so validation cannot turn a valid non-zero direction into zero through float overflow.
